newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU-Mexico trade deal held up over maritime cargo.
newsitem.headline: EU-Mexico trade deal held up over maritime cargo.

text.p: A long-awaited trade treaty between the European Union and Mexico was rejected by the EU on Wednesday because of a row over maritime cargo.

EU sources told Reuters that a meeting of ambassadors from the 15-nation bloc decided to send the treaty back to the European Commission for partial renegotiation after Denmark and Greece complained their shippers faced discrimination.

The ambassadors said the Commission needed to get assurances from Mexico that EU shippers would have the opportunity to operate on the same terms as other nations with whom Mexico has signed trade deals.
The EU-Mexico trade deal has long-been held up but last month appeared to be nearing conclusion after Mexico agreed to EU demands for a now-standard human rights clause in the treaty.

The source said the maritime obstacle was "not expected to be a showstopper", but could nevertheless irritate the Mexican government which has been criticised at home for bowing to EU demands for the rights clause. -- David Fox, Brussels Newsroom ++ 32 2 287 6832
